title: policy-enforcer-daemon: continuous residency assertions and evidence exporter
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a lightweight, deployable policy-enforcer daemon that continuously asserts data residency and retention configuration against policy-as-code, detects configuration drift, performs safe remediation when allowed, and emits cryptographically verifiable evidence bundles for audits.
background: Customers running Redwood Private and Dedicated have asked for an automated way to ensure their residency and retention configs do not drift from approved policies. Current controls are manual and produce ad-hoc evidence. This ticket designs and implements an agent that closes the loop: policy evaluation -> drift detection -> remediation workflow -> signed evidence export stored to audit buckets.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon runs as a sidecar or standalone pod on Private and Dedicated deployments and evaluates policies every configured interval
Policies authored in the company policy-as-code repo (OPA/rego) are compiled to WASM and loaded into the daemon at startup or via hot reload
Detected drift is classified (safe-auto-heal | needs-approval | informational) according to policy metadata
Safe-auto-heal remediation executes a documented set of idempotent ops (patch API/config) with backout TTL and produces a remediation event in audit log
All assertions and remediation actions are exported as an evidence bundle (JSONL + signed manifest) and pushed to customer audit buckets (S3/GCS) with KMS envelope encryption
Evidence bundles include before/after diffs, OPA policy version, daemon version, UTC timestamps, and a signed attest statement that verifies using the platform public key
Console shows per-customer compliance status, recent drift events, remediation actions, and a link to evidence bundles
Automated tests cover policy evaluation, drift classification heuristics, remediation rollback logic, and evidence bundle signing/verification
tasks: Design daemon architecture and failure modes (Maya)
Spec policy metadata schema (classification, auto-heal flags, remediation playbook)
Implement WASM policy loader and evaluation harness (Ethan)
Integrate with runtime config API for reading and patching residency/retention fields
Create evidence bundle format and signing workflow (KMS integration)
Add console endpoints and UX for per-customer status and evidence download
Add metrics/tracing: policy_evals_total, drift_detected_total, remediation_attempts, remediation_success_total
End-to-end tests and canary rollout plan
implementation_notes: Core policy engine: OPA compiled to WASM to run in both hosted control plane and customer-side daemon without lang/runtime dependency
Policy metadata will live in policies repo and include fields: 'scope', 'severity', 'auto_heal': ['never'|'safe'|'always'], 'remediation_playbook' (list of steps), 'audit_tags'
Daemon supports two modes: 'assert-only' (detect + report) and 'assert-and-heal' (attempt remediation). Default is assert-only for initial rollouts
Remediation runbook will use optimistic concurrency tokens when patching configs to avoid race conditions with other operators
Remediation actions are recorded to the customer audit log and produce an immutable event containing the diff and a signed attestation
Evidence bundles are rotated daily and retained according to customer retention policy; ability to query bundles by time range and policy id
Signed attestations use KMS envelope encryption; public key is published in the console for offline verification
Daemon will emit a structured event to pubsub/webhook for downstream SIEM integration
Provide a 'dry-run' flag that simulates remediation and includes proposed diffs in evidence bundles without changing configs
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Architecture draft completed and reviewed by Reliability. Chosen OPA->WASM approach for portability.
2025-01-20: Basic WASM loader and evaluation harness implemented. Running sample residency policy against local config fixtures.
2025-01-27: Evidence bundle format (JSONL + manifest) agreed with Compliance; draft signer implemented against dev KMS keyring.
2025-02-02: Integrated basic remediation shim that emits patch requests to runtime-config API. Enabled dry-run mode for safety.
2025-02-08: Console endpoints and link to evidence retrieval API scaffolded; front-end PM added initial wireframes (see artifacts).
review_feedback: Security: Require HSM-backed signing in prod; store minimal plaintext in bundles; redact PII by default
Product: Provide opt-in auto-heal per-customer and per-policy; enforce canary rollout for auto-heal across dedicated clusters
Design: Evidence download UX must include verification instructions and public-key fingerprint
Reliability: Add exponential backoff and circuit breaker for remediation attempts; emit alerts when remediation fails repeatedly
qa_plan: Simulate drift scenarios (misconfigured residency label, retention too short) and validate classification and evidence bundles
Verify dry-run remediation includes correct diffs and does not alter runtime configs
Run attacker scenarios to ensure daemon cannot escalate privileges when remediating
Verify evidence bundle signature verification using published public key
Load test evaluation cadence to ensure policy evaluations scale to 10k evaluations/min on Dedicated clusters
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood on staging clusters in assert-only mode
Phase 2: Opt-in customers for assert-only mode with evidence export to their audit buckets
Phase 3: Limited canary of assert-and-heal on 3 enterprise customers with manual approvals
Phase 4: Wide release with auto-heal opt-in and default backoff/TTL safety guards
observability: Metrics: policy_eval_duration_seconds (histogram), policy_evals_total, drift_detected_total, remediation_attempts_total, remediation_failures_total
Traces: end-to-end trace from evaluation -> remediation -> evidence upload
Dashboards: per-customer compliance status, top failing policies, remediations by outcome
security_considerations: KMS/HSM required for signing in prod; rotate keys quarterly
Evidence bundles must be encrypted at rest and access-controlled via IAM
Policy execution sandboxing: WASM runtime with memory limits and no filesystem/network by default
Auditability: every remediation action requires a signed event and a trace id linked to console action or operator identity
